templates.text: A sentence is the largest syntactic unit and sentences occur in sequence in a text without generally being contained in one another; a clause is a construction of subject plus predicate (in central cases) and can be embedded inside a larger one.
templates.deep_text: Applies when deciding whether a stretch of text is a sentence or a clause: it is a sentence only if it is one of the units occurring in succession in a text, and a clause if it has subject-predicate structure in the central cases; the same string can be a sentence in one text and merely part of a sentence in another. The current node is labelled {label} and spans “{surface}”. This Cambridge terminology note does not relabel the B-R tree or decide grammatical correctness.

templates.text: S → NP VP. Subject = the NP immediately dominated by S; predicate = the VP immediately dominated by S.

templates.text: Add “to” before the verb that follows passive “made”. For example, “They made us wait” becomes “We were made to wait”.
templates.deep_text: In the passive form, the person affected by “made” becomes the subject. The verb that follows “made” needs “to”, as in “were made to wait”.
